data.name: Dhaneswar
data.gender_notes: Dhaneswar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dhaneswar is derived from two Sanskrit words: Dhan (wealth) and Ishwar (God). This name is often used to honor the Hindu deity Ganesha, who is considered the lord of wealth and prosperity. The name Dhaneswar carries the meaning “God of wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhaneswar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dhaneswar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhaneswar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Dhaneswar Temple, also known as Dhaneswar Mahadev or Dhenkanal Temple, is a famous Shiva temple located in the Dhenkanal district of Odisha, India. The temple is believed to have been established during the 16th century by King Dhaneswar Dev, a ruler of the Khariar-Satkosia kingdom.

historical_references.reference: Another reference suggests that the name Dhaneswar might be derived from the Sanskrit words 'Dhan' (wealth) and 'Ishwar' (God), indicating the temple as the 'God of Wealth'. On YouTube, there are various devotional songs, prayers, and rituals dedicated to Lord Dhaneswar, reflecting the strong spiritual connection people have with the name.
